entries.title: Judges 11:2
segments:
A strange woman; not the lawful wife of his father. 
 
As the sins of parents may greatly injure and distress their children, this should be a motive to induce them to govern all their appetites and passions, and to regulate their whole conduct according to the revealed will of God.

entries.title: Judges 11:3
segments: The land of Tob; supposed to be in or near Syria.

entries.title: Judges 11:7
segments: In prosperity men often despise and reject those to whom in adversity they are glad to apply for help.

entries.title: Judges 11:9
segments: Arrangements in which different parties are concerned should be plainly and correctly stated beforehand, that there may be afterwards no misunderstandings and contests about them.

entries.title: Judges 11:10
segments: The Lord be witness; this was a solemn engagement that they would make Jephthah their ruler.

entries.title: Judges 11:11
segments: All his words; the words of the engagement between him and the elders of Gilead, that the people might all hear, understand, and ratify them.

entries.title: Judges 11:12
segments: For the wicked courses which wicked men pursue they can give no good reason; and a correct statement of facts shows that for their pretended reasons there is no just foundation.

entries.title: Judges 11:13
segments: Israel took away my land;

entries.title: Judges 11:21
segments: The agency of God should never be excluded in our contemplations of the affairs of men, and his goodness should always be acknowledged as the source of all the blessings which we enjoy.

entries.title: Judges 11:22
segments: The coasts of the Amorites; the Amorites had dispossessed the Ammonites and taken their country, from Arnon to Jabbok, before the children of Israel came out of Egypt; and the Israelites took it not from the Ammonites, to whom they ascribed their successes.

entries.title: Judges 11:24
segments: Chemosh; the idol-god of the Ammonites, to whom they ascribed their successes.

entries.title: Judges 11:25
segments: Better than Balak; had they any better claim to the lands than had Balak, who was king of Moab when Israel took them?  He did not take them back; and as the Ammonites had not attempted it, but suffered the Israelites to possess it unmolested for three hundred years, it was evident that they had lost all title to it, and the Israelites did not wrong them in possessing it.

entries.title: Judges 11:27
segments:
The Lord--be judge; decide, by giving the victory to those who were right. 
 
A disposition in the use of proper means to commit all our concerns to the guidance and disposal of God, is a good preparation for obtaining his favor, and receiving from him all needed aid.

entries.title: Judges 11:29
segments:
The Spirit--came upon Jephthah; furnishing him with wisdom, courage, and all needful qualifications to conduct the war. 
 
  Over; through the places mentioned, to collect his army.

entries.title: Judges 11:31
segments:
Be the Lord's; devoted especially to his service. 
 
  And; some have translated this, or; supposing that what should come to meet Jephthah was to be a burnt-offering, if it were an object which the law allowed for that purpose; and if not, that it was to be devoted to God in some other way. 
 
We should be careful to promise nothing but what is practicable, lawful, and right, that all we promise may be faithfully performed.

entries.title: Judges 11:33
segments:
Aroer; a town near the river Arnon. 
 
  Minnith; a place north of Aroer, in the tribe of Reuben.

entries.title: Judges 11:35
segments: Opened my mouth; made a vow.

This life is a mixed scene of trials and mercies.  Great blessings are often followed by great distresses; and if uncalled of God and without good reason we have brought them upon ourselves, the poignancy of them is thereby increased.

entries.title: Judges 11:37
segments:
My virginity; that she was to live and die without being married and having children, which Jewish women very much regreted.  If, as some suppose, she was not literally offered to the Lord as a burnt-offering, it is plain, from the language of the sacred writer, that she was devoted to God in such a way as required her to remain unmarried and childless. 
 
  Fellows; female companions.

entries.title: Judges 11:39
segments:
According to his vow; he devoted her to the Lord in a manner consistent with his promise, whatever that was. 
 
  She knew no man; was never married, and had no children; a thing bewailed and lamented both by herself and her companions.

entries.title: Judges 11:40
segments: Lament; this word in the original means, to celebrate, or rehearse, and is so translated in
.  The daughters of Israel, from year to year, commemorated the case of Jephthah's daughter.
